claims.text: The proposed intervention is to increase FeCoNiCrAl feedstock size from 15–45 μm to 50–60 μm.
Using 50–60 μm feedstock will produce a thicker coating than using 15–45 μm feedstock.
Larger feedstock particles improve deposition efficiency.
Improved deposition efficiency from larger particles causes the increase in coating thickness.
Larger particles reduce oxidation during spraying.
The 50–60 μm feedstock will preserve coating integrity relative to the 15–45 μm baseline.
The 50–60 μm feedstock will preserve minimal as-sprayed oxidation relative to the baseline.
The larger-feedstock coating will have improved properties relative to the baseline coating.
The benefits of the intervention will remain effective during subsequent service as a bond coat in a thermal barrier coating system.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires coating properties and integrity to be preserved, whereas the falsification rule requires the properties to be significantly improved. A thicker coating with unchanged, adequately preserved properties would satisfy the hypothesis but could be classified as falsifying it under the stated rule.
